title: backlog.py cost: tokens per item, rolled up
goal: python3 _tools/backlog.py cost ID prints the item's own tokens (per model: requests, in, cw, cr, out; main and sub) and the sum over its descendants, for a task, subtask, story, bug, epic or sprint; descendants and sprint membership come from item files at HEAD and, for items deleted at sprint close, from their last version in git history; --runs lists each run's line apart (one worked attempt each), --format json gives the same numbers for other tools.

gates.question: Which accounting model do cost rollups use? Settle: tokens of a session that works two items; cache writes; research one item triggers for another; the kb's background runs; retries and failed experiments.
options: split: direct (inside the item's claim-to-done window), attributed (its subagents), shared (session tokens outside any window) and the session total, printed apart; cache writes reported apart, never amortised; research charged to the item that claims the research task; background runs as system overhead
direct only: tokens inside the item's windows, nothing attributed or shared
one number per item, shared tokens split evenly between the items of a session
gates.recommendation: split: direct (inside the item's claim-to-done window), attributed (its subagents), shared (session tokens outside any window) and the session total, printed apart; cache writes reported apart, never amortised; research charged to the item that claims the research task; background runs as system overhead

notes: Resolving deleted items: git log --all -- kb/_self/backlog/<id>.json, then git show <commit>^:kb/_self/backlog/<id>.json (backlog.md, The item file). Tokens only, no price table. A task's sprint is its story's or bug's.
